title: India's Freedom Struggle in Brief
summary: A short story of how Indians worked together to end British rule and win independence in 1947.

steps.title: Before independence
sentences: For about two hundred years large parts of India were ruled by the British East India Company and then the British Crown.
Many Indians were unhappy because of heavy taxes, unfair laws and loss of freedom.
The uprising of 1857 was one of the first big revolts.

steps.title: Many paths
sentences: In 1885 the Indian National Congress was formed.
Leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal asked for self-rule.
Revolutionaries like Bhagat Singh, Chandra Shekhar Azad and Subhas Chandra Bose also worked for freedom in their own ways.

steps.title: Gandhi and non-violence
sentences: Mahatma Gandhi led movements based on non-violence and truth, such as the Non-Cooperation Movement, the Salt March in 1930 and the Quit India Movement in 1942.
Millions of ordinary people took part, including women and young people.
Leaders from Tamil Nadu such as V. O. Chidambaram Pillai and Subramania Bharati also played big roles.

steps.title: Independence
sentences: The country was also divided, and many people suffered during the partition.
Jawaharlal Nehru became the first Prime Minister, and we remember the freedom fighters every year.

facts: The Dandi Salt March in 1930 covered about 390 kilometres on foot.
Subramania Bharati's songs inspired many people during the freedom struggle.
Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi and Velu Nachiyar of Sivaganga were among the brave women who fought British rule.

quiz.q: Which march did Gandhi lead in 1930?
quiz.why: The Salt March to Dandi was in 1930.
The Quit India Movement was launched in 1942.

notes: Condensed summary for young readers. Topics such as partition are described briefly and sensitively.
